mechanism_of_action.value: Inhibits Na-K ATPase ('sodium pump'), increasing intracellular calcium in the myocardium and conduction system (positive inotropy, increased automaticity, reduced AV nodal conduction velocity) and indirectly stimulating parasympathetic activity at the SA and AV nodes while deactivating sympathetic and renin-angiotensin tone.

refs.quote: All of digoxin’s actions are mediated through its effects on Na-K ATPase. This enzyme, the “sodium pump,” is responsible for maintaining the intracellular milieu throughout the body by moving sodium ions out of and potassium ions into cells.

Digoxin is a substrate of P-glycoprotein, at the level of intestinal absorption, renal tubular section and biliary-intestinal secretion. Therefore, drugs that induce/ inhibit P-glycoprotein have the potential to alter digoxin pharmacokinetics.
The metabolism of digoxin is not dependent upon the cytochrome P-450 system, and digoxin is not known to induce or inhibit the cytochrome P-450 system.

Digoxin has a narrow therapeutic index, increased monitoring of serum digoxin concentrations and for potential signs and symptoms of clinical toxicity is necessary when initiating, adjusting, or discontinuing drugs that may interact with digoxin.

tier.note: Decades of retrospective clinical studies and case reports have not identified a drug-associated risk of major birth defects or miscarriage, and untreated maternal heart failure or AFib carries significant risk. However, animal reproduction studies have not been conducted, digoxin crosses the placenta, dose requirements may increase in pregnancy and decrease postpartum, and arrhythmia risk may increase during labor and delivery.

refs.quote: Experience with digoxin in pregnant women over several decades, based on published retrospective clinical studies and case reports, has not led to the identification of a drug associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage or adverse maternal and fetal outcomes.

Digoxin has been shown to cross the placenta and is found in amniotic fluid. Monitor neonates for signs and symptoms of digoxin toxicity, including vomiting, and cardiac arrhythmias [see Warnings and Precautions (5.3)] .
